gloss: injustice, wrong; act wrongly; give suck, suckling
summary: One spelling for two groups of words. The larger is wrong done against what is right: עָוֶל and עַוְלָה are injustice in judgment and in weights and measures, and wrongdoing set against righteousness, truth and uprightness; עַוָּל is the wrongdoer, and the rare piel is to act wrongly. Scripture says repeatedly that Yahweh has no עָוֶל, and Ezekiel that the righteous who turns to it dies in it. The smaller group is of the nursing young: the verb עוּל is used of ewes and cows giving suck, the noun עוּל is the suckling, and עֲוִיל a young child. Arabic ʿāla, of a judge or a balance that deviates from the right, matches the first; Ugaritic, Punic, Ge'ez and Aramaic words for suckling or foal match the second.

words.summary: The feminine form of עָוֶל, the commoner of the two in poetry. Spelled also עֹלָה, plural עוֹלֹת (Psa 58:3; 64:7), and once by transposed letters עַלְוָה (Hos 10:9).

senses.definition: Wrong done against what is right and true: what was found in the king of Tyre when he ceased to be blameless, what is not on the lips of a faithful teacher, and what Yahweh does not do.

evidence.note: “You were blameless (תָּמִים) in your ways from the day you were created, until עַוְלָתָה was found in you.”
“The instruction of truth (אֱמֶת) was in his mouth, and עַוְלָה was not found on his lips”: wrong set against truth and uprightness.
“Yahweh is righteous in her midst; he does not do עַוְלָה … yet the עַוָּל knows no shame.”
“With Yahweh our God there is no עַוְלָה, nor lifting of faces, nor taking of a bribe”: wrong in judgment, beside partiality and bribery.
Those who do not practise עַוְלָה “walk in his ways”.
“Yahweh is upright, my rock, and there is no עַוְלָתָה in him.”
“Who has said to him, You have done עַוְלָה?”
“Building Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with עַוְלָה.”
“He who sows עַוְלָה will reap trouble.”
“The remnant of Israel will not do עַוְלָה, nor speak a lie.”
Plural עוֹלֹת: “in heart you work wrongs; on the earth you weigh out the violence of your hands.”
Spelled עֹלָתָה: “the poor has hope, and עֹלָתָה shuts her mouth”; so Psa 107:42.

senses.definition: Injustice on the tongue: false and deceitful speech.

evidence.note: “My lips shall not speak עַוְלָה, nor my tongue utter deceit (רְמִיָּה).”
“Will you speak עַוְלָה for God, and speak deceit (רְמִיָּה) for him?”
“Your lips have spoken falsehood (שֶׁקֶר), your tongue mutters עַוְלָה.”
“From a man of deceit (מִרְמָה) and עַוְלָה deliver me.”

senses.definition: בֶּן עַוְלָה, “son of wrong”, is the violent oppressor who afflicts the weak; the phrase names Abner's murderers and those Yahweh promises will no longer afflict Israel or David's seed.

evidence.note: “I will plant him, and he will dwell in his own place … and sons of עַוְלָה will no longer afflict him as before.” So 1Ch 17:9.
David over Abner: “As one falls before sons of עַוְלָה, you fell”, of a man killed by treachery.
Of David: “an enemy shall not exact from him, nor a son of עַוְלָה afflict him.”
Spelled עַלְוָה: war will overtake the sons of עַלְוָה in Gibeah, recalling Gibeah's outrage (Jdg 19–20).

evidence.locator: 2Sa.7.10, עַוְלָה → ἀδικίας; 2Ch.19.7, עַוְלָה → ἀδικία; Psa.92.16, עַוְלָתָה → ἀδικία

evidence.note: “Is there unrighteousness (ἀδικία; Peshitta ʿawlā) with God? Far be it”: the denial of 2Ch 19:7 and Psa 92:16.

evidence.locator: Psa.89.23, עַוְלָה → ἀνομίας; Psa.107.42, עַוְלָה → ἀνομία

parallels.note: Blood: the city built with bloodshed is built with עַוְלָה.

opposites.note: Truth in the mouth, and no עַוְלָה on the lips.

phrases.gloss: sons of wrong: oppressors, violent men

senses.definition: Wrong done in judging or in trade: favouring one party, or a false measure or weight.

evidence.note: “You shall do no עָוֶל in judgment; you shall not lift the face of the poor nor honour the face of the great; in righteousness you shall judge your neighbour.”
“You shall do no עָוֶל in judgment, in measure, in weight, or in quantity”; and v. 36 calls for just balances.
After the law of honest weights and measures (vv. 13–15): “all who do עָוֶל are an abomination to Yahweh your God.”
“How long will you judge עָוֶל and lift the faces of the wicked?”
The righteous man “withholds his hand from עָוֶל, executes true judgment between man and man.”
“By the עֶוֶל of your trade you profaned your sanctuaries.”

senses.definition: Wrong as the opposite of righteousness and uprightness: what Yahweh is without, and what the righteous man who turns from his righteousness does and dies in.

evidence.note: “The Rock, his work is perfect, for all his ways are justice; a God of faithfulness and without עָוֶל, righteous and upright is he.”
“When a righteous man turns from his righteousness and does עָוֶל, and dies for it, in his עָוֶל that he has done he shall die.”
“A man of עָוֶל is an abomination to the righteous, and one upright in the way is an abomination to the wicked.”
“Far be it from God to do wickedness (רֶשַׁע), and from the Almighty to do עָוֶל.”
“What עָוֶל did your fathers find in me, that they went far from me?”
The wicked who turns, walking in the statutes of life “without doing עָוֶל”, “shall surely live, he shall not die.”
“If there is עָוֶל in my hands.”
“If I have done עָוֶל, I will do it no more.”

evidence.locator: Deu.32.4, עָוֶל → ἀδικία; Psa.7.4, עָוֶל → ἀδικία; Ezk.18.24, עָוֶל → ἀδικίαν

evidence.note: “He who seeks the glory of him who sent him is true, and there is no unrighteousness (ἀδικία) in him”: said of Jesus as Deu 32:4 says it of God.

parallels.note: Wickedness, which God does not do.

opposites.note: The righteous man turns from his righteousness and does עָוֶל.
Upright, set against the man of עָוֶל and the God without it.

senses.definition: Of ewes and cows, to suckle young: always the feminine participle עָלוֹת, “nursing ones”, the mothers whose young are still at the teat.

evidence.note: “Two nursing (עָלוֹת) cows … and bring their calves home away from them”: the cows have calves at the teat.
“The flocks and herds that are nursing (עָלוֹת) are with me”: driven hard, they and their young would die.
“He gathers the lambs in his arm and carries them in his bosom; he gently leads the nursing ones.”
“From following the nursing ewes he brought him to shepherd Jacob his people.”

words.summary: BDB's key for this noun (p.bg.ab) also gathers hundreds of tokens of the preposition עַל, so it is left off and the word's uses are counted by hand: Isa 49:15 and 65:20.

senses.definition: A child still at the breast.

evidence.note: “Can a woman forget her עוּל, so as not to have compassion on the son of her womb? Even these may forget, yet I will not forget you.”
“There shall no more be from there an עוּל of days, nor an old man who does not fill his days”: an infant who lives only days.

senses.definition: One who does עָוֶל, set beside the wicked and opposite Yahweh who is righteous.

evidence.note: “Yahweh is righteous in her midst; he does no עַוְלָה … but the עַוָּל knows no shame.”
“Let my enemy be as the wicked (רָשָׁע), and he who rises against me as the עַוָּל.”
“Is not calamity for the עַוָּל, and disaster for the workers of iniquity?”
Job broke the jaws of the עַוָּל and snatched the prey from his teeth: the oppressor of the poor.

words.summary: Only in Job, and only twice; it answers to עוּל “suckling”.

senses.definition: A young child, one of the little ones of a household.

evidence.note: “They send out their עֲוִילִים like a flock, and their children (יְלָדִים) dance.”
“Even עֲוִילִים despise me”: the least of all now scorn Job.
“Let favour be shown to the wicked, he will not learn righteousness; in the land of uprightness he will act wrongly (יְעַוֵּל).”
“Deliver me from the hand of the wicked, from the grasp of the one acting wrongly (מְעַוֵּל) and the ruthless.”

words.summary: Once, in Job 16:11; spelled as the noun “young child”, but the parallel “wicked” shows it is עַוָּל in another form.

senses.definition: An unjust man, parallel to the wicked.

evidence.note: “God delivers me to the עֲוִיל, and casts me into the hands of the wicked (רְשָׁעִים).”
“A resurrection of the dead, both of the righteous and of the unrighteous (ἀδίκων; Peshitta ʿawwālē).”

senses.definition: Wrongdoing, the opposite of God's righteousness and truth.

evidence.note: “Is there ʿawlā with God? Far be it.”
“He is true, and there is no ʿawlā in his heart.”
“The judge of ʿawlā”: the unjust judge.
He cleanses “from all our ʿawlā”.
“All ʿawlā is sin.”

senses.definition: Unrighteous, said of people and denied of God.

evidence.note: He sends rain “on the righteous and on the ʿawwālē”.
“A resurrection of the dead, of the righteous and of the ʿawwālē.”
“God is not ʿawwāl, to forget your work.”
“The ʿawwālē will not inherit the kingdom of God.”

senses.definition: Wrongdoing, in a list of sins.

evidence.note: First in the list: “filled with all ʿawwālūtā …”.

senses.definition: To do wrong, or to wrong another.

evidence.note: “Friend, I do you no wrong (lā maʿwel); did you not agree with me for a denarius?”
“We have wronged no one.”
“He who does wrong, let him do wrong still.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's word for the colt of Zec 9:9 in the gospels (Hebrew עַיִר); it is the young of the nursing animals.

evidence.note: Zec 9:9 quoted: “riding on an ass, and on a ʿīlā, the foal of an ass.”
“You will find an ass tied, and a ʿīlā with her.”

cognates.gloss: (of a balance) incline, fall short; (of a judge) deviate from the right course, act wrongfully
cognates.note: The same two settings as the Hebrew: the false balance (Lev 19:35–36; Deu 25:13–16) and the judge who wrongs (Lev 19:15; Psa 82:2). Arabic shows ʿ behind ע.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2200, art. عول, عَالَ (n31059)
evidence.note: “The balance inclined, or declined … it was, or became, defective, and declined from the right state … [hence] He was, or became, unfaithful [in the balance] … He (a judge) deviated from the right course, or acted wrongfully, in the judgment.”

cognates.note: The Targum's word in Deu 32:4, “without ʿawlā”.

evidence.locator: s.v. עַוְלָא, P00245, Targum Pseudo-Jonathan Deuteronomy 32:4 and Targum Proverbs 13:11
s.v. עַוָּלָא, P00246, Targum Proverbs 29:27, Targum Job 18:21, Targum Zephaniah 3:5
evidence.note: “Pervert; wrong-doer.” The Targum uses it for the Hebrew עַוָּל of Job 18:21 and Zep 3:5.

cognates.gloss: feed, nourish, sustain one's household; (ʿiyāl) the dependants one feeds
cognates.note: Feeding dependants, close to giving suck but not the same; in the same Arabic root as ʿāla “deviate”, so if it belongs here, Arabic too has both senses under ʿ.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2200, art. عول, عَالَ عِيَالَهُ (n31059)
evidence.note: “He fed, nourished, or sustained, his family, or household.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2201, art. عول, عِيَالٌ (n31070)
evidence.note: “A man's عِيَال are the persons whom he feeds, nourishes, or sustains.”

cognates.note: Listed by Anderson and Moser under *ʿwl “suck”; Ugaritic writes ʿ, not ġ. Not yet checked in a Ugaritic dictionary.

evidence.locator: p. 367, ʿL I, CIS I 198, lines 1–5
evidence.note: “Mago vowed his nursing son (ʿl) Idnibal”; Krahmalkov compares Hebrew עוּל.

evidence.locator: s.v. עוּלָא I, P00247, Bava Batra 9a
evidence.note: “Infant, nursling, child … the suckling that confounded its mother's way”; plural עוּלִין “foals”.

cognates.gloss: foal, young of an ass, horse or camel
cognates.note: The Ge'ez Bible's word for the foal of Zec 9:9 and of the gospels, as the Peshitta's ʿīlā is.

evidence.locator: s.v. ዕዋል (TraCES entry 7220), citing Zec 9:9 and Mat 21:2
evidence.note: “pullus asini, equi, cameli … in specie pullus asini.”

doctrine.statement: Moses' song says of Yahweh, “a God of faithfulness and without עָוֶל, righteous and upright is he” (Deu 32:4); Zephaniah, “Yahweh is righteous in her midst; he does not do עַוְלָה” (Zep 3:5); the psalm, “there is no עַוְלָה in him” (Psa 92:16); and Jehoshaphat told his judges, “with Yahweh our God there is no עַוְלָה, nor lifting of faces, nor taking of a bribe” (2Ch 19:7). Elihu says the same (Job 34:10), and Yahweh asks Israel what wrong their fathers found in him (Jer 2:5). The law asks the same of Israel's judges and traders: no עָוֶל in judgment, no favour to poor or great, no false weight (Lev 19:15, 35; Deu 25:16). Paul asks, “Is there unrighteousness with God?” and answers, “Far be it” (Rom 9:14), and Hebrews, “God is not unjust to forget your work” (Heb 6:10). From the verses: Yahweh's judgment never deviates from the right, and those who judge for him are to judge as he does.

Ezekiel states the outcome of עָוֶל in plain terms: “when a righteous man turns from his righteousness and does עָוֶל … in his עָוֶל that he has done he shall die” (Ezk 18:26; so 3:20; 18:24; 33:13, 18), while the wicked man who turns and walks in the statutes of life “without doing עָוֶל … shall surely live, he shall not die” (Ezk 33:15). The same chapter says, “the soul (נֶפֶשׁ) that sins, it shall die” (Ezk 18:4). From the verses: the end of wrongdoing is death, the end of the life itself, and life is set before the one who turns from it; nothing in them speaks of a soul living on after the death they name.

Paul's hope before Felix was “that there will be a resurrection of the dead, both of the righteous and of the unrighteous” (Act 24:15; Peshitta ʿawwālē), and he warned that “the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom of God” (1Co 6:9). From the verses: the unrighteous of whom he speaks are raised to face judgment, and the kingdom of God is the inheritance they are shut out of; the inheritance is received at the resurrection, not at death.

In the covenant with David Yahweh promised, “I will appoint a place for my people Israel and will plant them, that they may dwell in their own place and be disturbed no more, and sons of עַוְלָה shall no longer afflict them as before” (2Sa 7:10; 1Ch 17:9), and of David's seed, “a son of עַוְלָה shall not afflict him” (Psa 89:23). Zephaniah foresees the day when “the remnant of Israel shall not do עַוְלָה nor speak lies … and none shall make them afraid” (Zep 3:13). From the verses: the promise is of Israel planted in its own land, free of oppressors, under David's son, with a people who do no wrong; Israel was afflicted and exiled after it was given, so it waits for that son's reign.

note: Drafted 2026-11-18. Two groups in one spelling: injustice (Arabic ʿāla, ʿ) and suckling/young (Ugaritic ʿl per Anderson–Moser, ʿ). Both show ʿ, so the split is in meaning only, unless Arabic غيل ġayl “milk of a woman suckling while pregnant” (Lane p. 2318, n32763, n32767), a lead with ġ, is the suckling cognate; it is left out because the Ugaritic writes ʿ. Check Ugaritic ʿl in DULAT (not consulted) and decide whether Arabic ʿāla “sustain one's household” is the true suckling cognate. Left in other entries: עוֹלֵל/עוֹלָל “little child” and the Peshitta's עֻולָא “baby” (Luk 1:41; 2:12) stay in alal.json, with the Punic ʿl there too; this entry cites the Punic again for עוּל. עֹל “yoke” stays in alal.json. BDB key overlaps: p.bi.ab (עָוֶל) and p.bi.ad (עַוְלָה) list largely the same tokens, so their counts include each other and are not word totals; p.bi.ad also gathers Gen 36:40, 1Ch 1:51 (the Edomite chief Alvah/Aliah, root unclear, no name file) and Deu 27:6 (עֹלֹת “burnt offerings”, of עלה). The noun עוּל's key p.bg.ab gathers 500+ tokens of the preposition עַל and is left off; its real uses are Isa 49:15 and 65:20, and BDB would read it at Job 24:9 (“they take the suckling of the poor in pledge”), where the translation reads the preposition וְעַל; not cited. Isa 61:8 בְּעוֹלָה is pointed “with burnt offering”; MACULA lemmatizes it עַוְלָה (“robbery with wrong”); not cited. SEDRA's verb lexeme 2271 also tags עֻול “enter!” at Mat 6:6; 25:21, 23; Act 9:6, which belong to עלל (alal); only Mat 20:13, 2Co 7:2 and Rev 22:11 are this root's aphel. Ge'ez ዕዋል cited by entry, column not checked in the print. Payne Smith not consulted for Syriac outside the Peshitta. No clear personal name from the root.
